title: test(grid): pin the member shape of object-grid columns, filter, grouping and sort (objectui#8071 slice 17)
body:
Refs #8071

Clause-②: no

objectui#8071 **slice 17** — the four remaining `object-grid` member-pin exemptions
(`columns`, `filter`, `grouping`, `sort`) become named per-block pins, their exemption
entries are deleted and `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` moves with the list, in one
commit. ⭐ **The `object-grid` block CLOSES** — the largest block on this card, in its
fourth bite.

## The ledger, re-derived on this branch head

Every figure below is read by a TypeScript AST walk of
`apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`
(`ts.createSourceFile` → `VariableDeclaration` → initializer unwrapped through
`as` / `satisfies` / parens → `PropertyAssignment`, boundaries from node spans),
because four separate regex and brace-counting misreadings of this one file are on
the record. ⛔ None of it is copied from the dispatch order.

| reading | before (`4e27a9b6c7`) | after |
| --- | --: | --: |
| `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` | 8 | **4** |
| exemption keys, enumerated | 8 | **4** |
| `MEMBER_PINS` key lines | 83 | **87** |
| `NEWLY_JUDGED_UNPINNED_MEMBERS` | empty | empty |

Set arithmetic, balanced: −4 exemptions, −4 ceiling, +4 pins, and **4 = the ceiling**,
so the enumeration is the whole population rather than a sample. The four that remain:
`object-master-detail-form` 3 (`dataSource` · `details` · `fields`) ·
`record:related_list.actions` 1 (`NO_READ_SITE_TO_PIN`, ⛔ not re-measured here —
slice 7's measurement stands).

## The four pins

Two are **promoted pre-existing files**, each read end to end first and then GROWN by
the member dispositions it never stated. Two are new, because nothing existing stated
the member SET for either key.

| key | pin | new or promoted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridColumnMembers-8071.test.tsx` | new |
| `filter` | `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridFilterInputSpelling.test.tsx` | promoted + grown |
| `grouping` | `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridGroupingMembers-8071.test.tsx` | new |
| `sort` | `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridArrayArmOrderby-8973.test.tsx` | promoted + grown |

What each says, in one line apiece:

- **`columns`** — the eleven members the registration's prose elides, and the
  precedence between them: `label` outranks the machine-name prettifier, an authored
  `align` outranks the numeric-type inference, `type` outranks the NAME-shaped
  heuristic this block runs. ⭐ The two ways a column vanishes are pinned as
  different events — `hidden: true` is authored intent and is silent, while an
  unresolvable column is dropped AND reported (objectui#5349).
- **`filter`** — the three members of one `ViewFilterRule`: the operator alias fold,
  the verbatim escape for an operator the spec does not know, the 2-tuple an omitted
  `value` lowers to, and the render-time refusal an array comparand on a
  single-valued operator produces (the block is replaced by an alert naming the
  field; ⚠️ WHERE that lands is objectui#9050's question, not endorsed here).
- **`grouping`** — `fields` and its entries' `field` / `order` / `collapsed`, at the
  headers AND at the projection, with the unusable-entry set asserted equal on both
  sides.
- **`sort`** — `field` and `order` across ALL THREE readers this block has for them:
  the fetch join string, the export projection `{ field, direction }`, and the
  header-arrow reader `parseSchemaSort`.

### The shared memo, handled rather than re-flattened

Slice 16 measured `object-grid`'s four as separable **with the qualification** that
`grouping` and `columns` are not disjoint: one memo (`groupValueFormatter`) derives
the group-header labels from BOTH keys. This slice takes both, so the overlap is
pinned where it lives — in the `grouping` file, in its own `describe`, with each row
carrying an absent-member control so a failure still names one key. The `columns` pin
authors no `grouping` at all, which is what keeps the two ablation legs below
separable. `order` sorting the RENDERED labels is the sharpest consequence: a column
override MOVES the groups.

## Ablation A — the gate mechanism itself

One deleted exemption (`'object-grid.columns': AWAITING_A_PIN`) re-added, **the
ceiling untouched**.

On-disk proof, taken BEFORE any result was read:

```
HEAD blob: c46dfd735403b86776e2604a7f3fa1e34f0f03dc
disk blob: da359406802e80a832baedbe1a9d779543af62d1
count of INJECTED text on disk: 1
```

⚠️ This leg is an INSERTION, so there is no "removed text is gone" count to take —
the anchor it inserts before is still on disk by construction, and saying otherwise
would be a claim about nothing.

Result — `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`,
exit captured before any pipe: **3 failed | 196 passed (199)**

```
× judges a non-vacuous member-shape census …   expected [ 'object-grid.columns' ] to deeply equal []
× carries no stale member-pin exemption …      expected [ 'object-grid.columns' ] to deeply equal []
× the member-pin exemption list only ratchets DOWN   expected 5 to be less than or equal to 4
```

The third row is the one that proves the ceiling moved WITH the list rather than
beside it. Restored from a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` using absolute paths and
`git checkout HEAD -- path`; restoration is asserted **by blob hash**
(`c46dfd735403b86776e2604a7f3fa1e34f0f03dc`, equal to HEAD) and by an empty
`git diff HEAD`, ⛔ never by an exit code.

## Ablation B — one leg per new pin, all four pin files in ONE run each

Baseline, unmutated: **4 files, 50 tests passed**. Every leg mutates one read site,
proves the write on disk (injected count, removed count, and a `git hash-object`
differing from the HEAD blob) before any result is read, and restores under a trap
with the blob hash asserted equal afterwards.

| leg | read site mutated | red | green in the same run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `resolveColumnLabel(col.label)` dropped from the header chain | **1** — `` `label` OUTRANKS the machine name `` | the other 3 files |
| `grouping` | `const order = f.order ?? 'asc'` pinned to `'asc'` | **1** — `` `order: "desc"` reverses the header order `` | the other 3 files |
| `filter` | `toFilterNode(schemaFilterSource)` replaced by the raw source | **7**, all in the filter pin | the other 3 files |
| `sort` | `toOrderByClause` reverted to the pre-objectui#8973 bare interpolation | **9**, all in the sort pin | the other 3 files |

⭐ Two legs reddened MORE rows than one, and both are reported rather than tuned
away. Deleting the filter lowering removes the one hop every filter row observes, so
the whole key section goes with the member section — including the refusal row, which
needs the lowering to reach the throw. Reverting `toOrderByClause` reddens the legacy
`defaultSort` arm too, because objectui#8973 deliberately routed both arms through the
one normalizer; that neighbour going red is the shared implementation doing its job,
not a leak.

⛔ No dist preflight is claimed or needed: this repo's `vitest.config.mts` aliases every
`@object-ui/*` specifier to that package's `src`, so the mutated source IS what the run
resolved. The blob-hash proof is the instrument; ⛔ the editor's exit code is not.

## What was run, and what was not

| command | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-grid/` | 145 files, **1376 passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console test` | 101 files, **1158 passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid lint` | `0 errors, 875 warnings` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console lint` | `0 errors, 212 warnings` |
| eslint over the 5 changed files, `--format json` | 5 files, **0 errors**, 25 warnings |
| `check:new-line-citations` · `check:control-bytes` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · `check:unreferenced-sources` | exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` · `check-changeset-no-major` · `check-changeset-fixed` | exit 0 |

⚠️ The first `type-check` of `plugin-grid` exited **2** with `Cannot find module
'@object-ui/…'` — an unbuilt dependency closure, ⛔ not a red gate. Both closures were
built (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-grid^...' build`, same for console) and both
type-checks then exited 0.

⚠️ **The type-check leg that sees these files is the second one.** `plugin-grid`'s
`tsconfig.json` excludes `__tests__`: with `--listFiles`, the first leg lists **0** of
the two new files and the `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` leg lists **all four** pin files.
The console's own `tsc --noEmit` lists the ledger file (count 1).

⛔ **No green-head claim.** Repo-wide `pnpm lint` (`eslint .` over the whole tree) and
the full repository suite were NOT run here — they are CI's runs. The readings above
are the targeted ones, named individually so each can be re-derived.

## Acceptance notes

⚠️ **Two member facts are pinned as BEHAVIOUR and handed back as findings, ⛔ not
repaired here.** Both are class findings that need their own card; an assertion that
either can never change would have to be deleted before anyone could change it.

1. **`object-grid.sort[].order` reaches the export door UNNORMALIZED.** The fetch path
   and the header-arrow reader both fold anything that is not `desc` to `asc`; the
   server-streamed export projection reads `?? 'asc'` and passes the authored token
   through verbatim. One authored `{ field: 'name', order: 'descending' }` therefore
   orders the screen ascending, draws an ascending arrow, and asks `exportDownload`
   for `direction: 'descending'` — three answers from one member, with no diagnostic.
   Probe: the row `an UNRECOGNISED order is normalized for two readers and passed
   through by the third` in `gridArrayArmOrderby-8973.test.tsx`. Dedupe words:
   `object-grid` · `sort` · `order` · `direction` · `exportDownload` ·
   `unnormalized direction`.
2. **`groupValueFormatter` reads `columns[].options`, a member `ListColumnSchema`
   REFUSES.** That schema is strict and declares fourteen members; `options` is not
   one of them, so an author who writes it is rejected at publish with
   `unrecognized_keys` while this renderer honours it for the group-header labels —
   the `declared != enforced` split AGENTS.md #0.1 exists to stop, and the same family
   objectui#6458 retired from `generateColumns()`'s cell branch. `columnReadBoundary-6458`
   bounds THAT branch to the empty set; this memo is outside it. Probe: the row
   `an UNDECLARED columns[].options decides the header label too` in
   `gridGroupingMembers-8071.test.tsx`, with its no-`options` control. Dedupe words:
   `object-grid` · `columns` · `options` · `groupValueFormatter` ·
   `undeclared column member` · `ListColumnSchema strict`.

⛔ **No existing pin was weakened, softened or deleted.** objectui#9884 and
objectui#9885 are filed against `object-master-detail-form` and are expected to red
pins slice 15 landed — that fix and its pin belong to the same change, and that change
is theirs. This slice took `object-grid` and did not touch that block.

⚠️ **The named successor did NOT transfer here either.** The six cross-file
`ObjectForm.tsx` line-address citations in
`packages/plugin-form/src/masterDetailFormTypeVocabulary.test.tsx` pass to whichever
slice takes `object-master-detail-form`; this slice took `object-grid`, so its diff
never touches that file and an opportunistic repair would have been the sweep
AGENTS.md #11 forbids.

Noted, not filed: the `grouping` registration's one-sentence description names no
member at all, and `columns`' names two of fourteen. That is this card's whole subject
rather than a separate defect, and the carrier that will meet it next is objectui#8071's
own remaining block — so it is recorded here rather than as a card of its own.

## Changeset

`.changeset/member-pins-object-grid-slice-17.md`, EMPTY frontmatter — declared as
releasing nothing. `check-changeset-presence` names the reason in its own words:
three source files of two released packages changed and every changeset has an empty
frontmatter, which is the explicit exemption. Nothing under any package's published
`files[]` moves; the diff is test files plus the ledger.

⛔ This PR stays **draft** and does not close the card (`Refs`): no auto-merge, no
enqueue, no merge — the PM lands it.
